description:
FILED s484d (the harness family, 2026-09-14).  Found by writing
`run_multiple_progs` (#1652): the ported code commented its failure
diagnostic the way perl's own t/test.pl does, `$err_line =~ s/^/# /mg`, and
81 of op/tie.t's 95 TAP rows and 3 of op/anonsub.t's 15 DISAPPEARED from the
stream -- printed as `# not ok 4`.

THE RULE (perlre, /m): "^ will match after any newline within the string,
EXCEPT if the newline is the last character in the string".  PCL's regex
layer (cl-ppcre :multi-line-mode) has no such exception, so it offers one
extra match position at end-of-string.

REPRODUCER (scratch probe, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl -- both columns measured):

    my $n = () = $s =~ /^/mg;  my $blank = () = $s =~ /^$/mg;

    src        perl carets  PCL carets   perl /^$/  PCL /^$/
    "a\n"           1            2            0         1
    "a\n\n"         2            3            1         2
    "a\nb"          2            2            0         0
    ""              1            1            1         1
    "\n"            1            2            1         2

    my $t = "x\n"; $t =~ s/^/> /mg;
      perl: "> x\n"          PCL: "> x\n> "      <-- the stray prefix

WHAT IT BREAKS.  Only patterns that can match EMPTY at that position, which
is why it has survived this long: `/^foo/m` cannot match there.  The live
shapes are
  * `s/^/PREFIX/mg` on text ending in a newline -- appends PREFIX with no
    newline after it, so the next write to the same descriptor continues that
    line.  That is how a TAP row became a comment.
  * counting or matching blank lines with `/^$/mg` -- off by one for any text
    that ends in a newline.
  * anything else whose `^`-anchored pattern is fully optional.
`split /^/m` AGREES with perl (split discards the trailing empty field), and
`$` under /m agrees too (perl's `$` does match at end-of-string).

WHERE THE FIX GOES: the pattern translation in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (the
`%pcl-build-scanner` family), which hands `^` to cl-ppcre's multi-line mode.
The semantics wanted are "start of string, or after a newline that is not the
last character", i.e. `(?:\A|(?<=\n)(?!\z))` -- so this is a rewrite of the
`^` token when /m is in force, not a flag change.  MEASURE FIRST: it is a
regex-layer change, so per CLAUDE.md's WHAT-TO-RUN table it owes the full
sweep plus the re/ and op/ companion legs, and an emission A/B if the
translation is compile-time.  A cheap discriminating measurement before
designing: count how many `^`-anchored EMPTY-matchable patterns exist across
the four populations (`grep -a` for `s/\^/` and `/\^\$/`), which bounds the
blast radius.

THIS SESSION'S WORKAROUND (not a fix): perl-tests/t/test.pl's
run_multiple_progs comments its diagnostic with perl's own `_comment()` shape
-- `join '', map { "# $_\n" } split /\n/, $text` -- which has no `^` at all.
subject: `^` under /m matches ONE EXTRA TIME at the end of a string that ends in a newline -- perlre says it must not, and `s/^/# /mg` therefore appends a stray prefix that glues itself to the next thing written to the fd
